A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Shapley-interaction research, despite substantial retitling and revision. Text, equations, and figures are readable. V1 includes Appendices A and B; v2 ends after its references, allowing their removal to be established.

before.justification: V1 reports original interaction analyses of language, speech, and image models, plus multilingual subword and image-reference experiments in its appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports original language and speech interaction analyses, including positional, syntactic, multiword-expression, and phonetic results in Figures 1–5.

M1.justification: The normalized pairwise STII expression in Equation 3 remains unchanged, and v2 newly specifies Monte Carlo permutation sampling. However, its coalition-weight definition differs mathematically from v1. The PDFs do not establish whether this reflects an implemented attribution change or an error in the revised explanation.

E1.justification: V2 removes MNIST and CIFAR-100 image-classification studies and the English/German/Turkish multilingual subword experiments, including the GermEval and Turkish NER datasets. English WikiText language modeling and Common Voice speech analyses remain, substantially narrowing domain and language coverage.

E2.justification: The retained analyses use the same GPT-2, BERT-base-uncased, and wav2vec2-base-960h models. Strong-MWE, weak-MWE, and all-pair comparisons remain. Neither version benchmarks against competing attribution algorithms; removing the ViT and XLM-R studies removes applications rather than replacing comparators within retained experiments.

E3.justification: Section 3 changes stated sentence truncation from 50 to 20 tokens. Speech preprocessing changes from p2fa_py3/Penn Forced Aligner to Montreal Forced Aligner with its US ARPA acoustic model. These substantially revise the reported settings. V2's specification of 198 audio files is new disclosure, not sufficient evidence of a reduced sample.

E4.justification: V2 removes Appendix A's analyses of same-word subword interactions and their relationship to prediction loss. It also removes Appendix B's reference-value sensitivity investigation and spurious-eye case study, along with Section 5's local image reconstruction and pixel-region interaction analyses.

E5.justification: Retained uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged: Figure 2 uses p < 0.05 and requires at least 50 observations per included syntactic distance, while Figure 4 reports bootstrap confidence intervals. Neither version supplies repeated-run or seed counts. Changed interval values and removal of entire studies do not establish a changed statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 2 reverses the dominant syntax pattern: for example, the ALM cell at di=1, dp=4 changes from +0.02 to -0.08. Figure 3 now reports more consistent MWE elevation in both models. Speech values also change; v2 Figure 4 shows consonant-vowel interaction below consonant-consonant interaction at 0.04 seconds. Vision and multilingual results disappear. These are revised results under changed settings, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The foundational Shapley definition changes from v1 Equation 1's factorial weights to binomial-count weights in v2 Equations 1–2. These are not equivalent; v2's weights are unnormalized despite the accompanying description of a weighted average. The standalone Shapley-residual definition and image-local aggregation equation are also removed, while the normalized STII expression remains.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction reverse the principal syntax claim: v1 emphasizes stronger syntactic organization in masked models, whereas v2 attributes consistent syntactic interactions to autoregressive models. V2 also replaces the model-dependent MWE-distance claim with a broader shared finding and narrows the main contribution from text, speech, and vision to linguistic structure.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the masked-model hierarchy interpretation with explanations favoring autoregressive syntax and suggesting positional complications in masked models. It adds a semantic-versus-co-occurrence interpretation of strong/weak MWEs, phonemic-discretization and voicing arguments, and explicit limitations concerning correlation and small models. The subword-predictability and image-boundary interpretations are removed.

D1.justification: V2 newly identifies the permutation-sampling estimator and specifies 198 speech files totaling approximately 20 minutes, 16 kHz sampling, and the US ARPA alignment model. Conversely, v1's explicit statement that text tokens are ablated using padding tokens disappears. These change reproducibility documentation without establishing that every newly disclosed detail represents a changed implementation.

R1.justification: The expanded Background and Related Work section positions the study against behavioral evaluation, nonlinear probing, and causal interpretability, adding works such as Hu et al. (2024), Voita and Titov (2020), Geiger et al. (2021), and Arora et al. (2024). Ahuja et al. (2024) supports the revised syntax interpretation. Vision and multilingual references disappear with those studies.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, background, and speech explanations, and changes the title and author presentation. Related work moves into Section 2, the image section and both appendices disappear, and a dedicated Limitations section replaces the earlier Broader Impact discussion. This is extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: V1 Figures 6–10 are removed. Retained figures are substantially reformatted: Figures 1–2 become prominent full-width displays, Figure 3 changes from six to four prediction-distance panels per model, and Figure 5 is redrawn with different chart styling. Captions are extensively expanded, and the document adopts a different layout and header treatment.

improvement.justification: V2 improves explanations, research positioning, reproducibility details, and explicit limitations. However, it introduces non-equivalent, unnormalized Shapley weights in Equation 2, and Section 4.2 calls /g/ a very high-STII outlier although Figure 5 places it near the low end of the scale. The PDFs do not establish whether the weighting error affects the revised results. These benefits and unresolved reliability concerns prevent a confident net quality judgment.
